title: Supply-ramp startup time of the untrimmed core over the full PVT matrix
claim: README.md 'Target specification (DRAFT)' row 'Startup time' (< 1 ms), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Records are PROVISIONAL against the draft spec until issue #1 ratifies it. Ramps the supply feeding design/bandgap_core.sch from 0 V to the corner supply in t_ramp and measures the first time VREF rises through 1.08 V (90% of the 1.20 V draft nominal), open-circuit, over the full 45-point PVT matrix. NOTE: the core cell as merged by #8 contains no startup injector -- GDRV is exposed as the attachment node and the injector is issue #10's deliverable -- so this bench measures the core AS COMMITTED. A failure here is a statement about the missing injector, not about the bench.

analyses: meas tran vreffin FIND v(vref) AT=1.9m
meas tran vddfin FIND v(vdd) AT=1.9m
meas tran gdrvfin FIND v(gdrv) AT=1.9m

measurements.name: t_start_ms
measurements.note: Startup time: first time VREF rises through 1.08 V (90% of the 1.20 V draft nominal) after the supply ramp begins at t=0. Limit is the draft spec's < 1 ms row. Computed as minimum(time*up + (1-up)*1) so a core that never crosses the threshold reports the 1 s sentinel as 1000 ms -- a legible, loudly failing number -- instead of an undefined `meas ... WHEN` vector that would take every later measurement in the .control block down with it.

measurements.name: vref_final
measurements.note: VREF at 1.9 ms, i.e. 19 ramp time constants after the supply is up. Deliberately a wide degenerate-state guard, not the accuracy claim (that is sim/output-voltage-tc/): it asserts the core actually reached and held its intended operating point rather than crossing the threshold on a glitch. If the core stays in its zero-current state this reads ~0 V.

measurements.name: gdrv_final
measurements.note: PMOS mirror gate / startup attachment node at 1.9 ms. The all-off degenerate solution parks this node at VDD (>= 2.97 V anywhere in the supply range), so an upper bound of 2.9 V excludes that state at every corner. This is the measurement that names the failure mode when startup does not happen.

measurements.name: vdd_final
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the supply ramp actually completed and is holding the corner's supply value at 1.9 ms. The window spans all three supply endpoints (2.97 / 3.30 / 3.63 V); a ramp that never got off the ground would read ~0 V and invalidate every number above.

measurements.name: n_tran_points
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the transient really produced a populated waveform (the 5 us max timestep over 2 ms floors this at 400 points). A transient that aborted after a handful of timepoints would make minimum(tcand) meaningless.

spread_checks.note: The settled supply must move by at least 0.5 V across the matrix (2.97 -> 3.63 V is 0.66 V). This is the corner-liveness check for this bench: it proves the runner's supply knob reaches the simulator. It is deliberately NOT placed on t_start_ms or vref_final -- if the core does not self-start, those are pinned at their sentinel/zero values by the physics under test, and a spread check on them would report a second, redundant failure that says nothing new.

notes: Full 45-point PVT matrix, no subset: startup is meaningful at every individual corner and a supply-ramp transient is affordable at every one of them.

t_ramp = 100 us is a single deck parameter so that ramp-rate sensitivity (slow vs fast ramps) can be swept without touching the schematic. Systematic ramp-rate variation and the no-other-stable-state initial-condition sweep are issue #10's acceptance criteria, not this issue's; this issue's spec line is the < 1 ms startup time itself.

No .nodeset in this testbench, unlike every sibling bench in the suite: seeding the DC solver onto the intended branch is exactly what this measurement must not do. The transient starts from the circuit's own t=0 solution with the supply at 0 V.

Open-circuit output. A capacitive load slows startup, so the recorded numbers are the optimistic case for the core; a loaded startup figure belongs with the output buffer, which this block does not have.

The comparison in `let up = (v(vref) gt 1.08)` uses ngspice's `gt` alias rather than `>`. In the ngspice command interpreter `>` is output redirection, so `let up = (v(vref) > 1.08)` is parsed as a redirect and fails with a syntax error -- which, because `up` then does not exist, silently takes the dependent measurement down with it. The alias form is the working one; do not 'tidy' it back to `>`.
